First-person pronouns show ergative alignment.
Second-person pronouns show ergative alignment.
Third-person pronouns show ergative alignment.
Full NP's exhibit ergative-absolutive alignment.
Clauses with imperfective aspect do  not exhibit ergative alignment.
Clauses with perfective aspect exhibit ergative alignment.
Past-tense clauses exhibit ergative alignment.
Clauses in non-past tense do not exhibit ergative alignment.
Clauses in indicative mode show an ergative alignment.
Clauses in non-indicative mode show an ergative alignment.
Clauses with realis status show ergative alignment.
Clauses with irrealis status show ergative alignment.
In the context of an agentive A argument, ergative alignment is observed.
In the context of a non-agentive argument A, ergative alignment is not observed.
In the context of a topical A, ergative alignment is shown.
In the context of a non-topical A, ergative alignment is shown.
Clauses with animated A arguments do exhibit ergative alignment.
Clauses with non-animated A arguments exhibit ergative alignment.
Main clauses do exhibit ergative alignment.
Non-main clauses exhibit ergative alignment.
The ergative mark is conditioned by the lexical semantics of the verb, specifically manifested in split intransitivity and in lexical exceptions of transitive verbs.
The ergative case does not have the same marker as the genitive case.
The ergative case does not have the same marker as the instrumental or comitative marker.
